نَحِيتٌ A comb: syn. مُشْطٌ or مَشْطٌ. (So in different copies of the K.) ＝
-A2- حَافِرٌ نَحِيتٌ A hoof of which the edges have gone [or become abraded, been worn away]; (S, K;) [and so ↓ حافر مَنْحَوتٌ , occurring in the K in art. حك, where, in its place in the S, we find حافر نَحِيتٌ.] ―
-b2- نَحِيتٌ (tropical:) An emaciated camel: (K:) a camel whose feet are worn, abraded, or wasted. (L.) ―
-b3- ↓ نَحِيتَةٌ A [portion of the] trunk of a tree, which is hewn out, and hollowed, in the form of a jar such as is called حُبّ, for bees: pl. نُحُتٌ. (L.) ―
-b4- نَحِيتٌ Anything bad; what is bad of anything. (L.) ＝
-A3- نَحِيتٌ One who introduces himself among a people, and lives with them, not being of their race. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
